per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window, indirect only: at 20 °C apo WT has the highest 15N R1 in the R78 loop (76-82) and residues 36-38 (J8; r3, r31); NADP+ binding lowers active-site R1 and raises it at the periphery (J18; r4, r34). No S2 or model-free fit exists. Not judged: hyrax R1 rows r44, r45.
per_window.us-ms: dynamic_in_window for apo WT at every temperature measured (0-20 °C): >30 residues at 20 °C with per-residue kex S111 1,200 ± 300 and L125 2,200 ± 540 s-1 (J1, r1), a per-residue refit of the same data (J2, r38), grouped Arrhenius fits for active-site Group II (1,088 s-1 at 20 °C to 181 s-1 at 0 °C) and C-terminal Group III (3,797 to 850 s-1) (J3, J4; r15-r18), a faster second process at T77-N79 (J6, r5) and R2>R1rho in the R78 loop and 164-177 (J7, r31). The adenine-site Group I does not exchange in apo (J5) but does once coenzyme binds. NADP+ at 20 °C quenches loop exchange (J17, r2) except S111, T164 and new D36-R39 (J16); at 0-10 °C the NADPH and NADP+ complexes show all three groups (J19, J20, J21, J22, J23, J24) and the NADP+/bilirubin complex loses Group II (J27). Mutants R78A, T164A/I/S and S111A change but do not remove exchange (inference_from_mutant); lemur and hyrax S164 are quenched (inference_from_homolog). Ligand signal loss with erythrosin B and phloxine B is multimerization (J29, artefact_suspected).
per_window.slower_than_ms: not_measured for apo conformational change (J13; HDX-MS, EPR/DEER, smFRET and time-resolved searched with no hits). ZZ-exchange coenzyme on/off rates (J15, J34) are ligand binding kinetics, recorded as unresolved and not counted here. Not judged: cellular nanoBRET inhibitor residence times r71-r73.
per_window.undetermined: Room-temperature apo crystal shows a disordered R78 loop (J9, r35, structure_only); the cryogenic crystal orders it through a lattice contact (J10, artefact_suspected); CS-Rosetta apo ensemble spread (J11, r9) and a 100 ns implicit-solvent MD from a holo start (J12, r49) carry no timescale; apo-versus-holo and inhibitor-complex structures show ligand-linked rearrangements at R35, R39, R78, W116, R170, R174 (J14, J31, J32). Not judged: redox-state filtered NOESY r46, r47; S111A/S111L MD r50, r51; inhibitor-bound MD r52, r57; abstract-only rows r64-r69.

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes: apo wild-type human BLVRB (20 °C, 50 mM Bis-Tris pH 6.5) shows fast-regime μs–ms exchange at more than 30 residues around the three active-site loops (10-15, 76-82, 109-114) and in the C-terminal lobe, with per-residue kex of 1,200 ± 300 s-1 at S111 and 2,200 ± 540 s-1 at L125 and a population that is not separable in fast exchange; grouped Arrhenius fits give 1,088 ± 180 s-1 (active-site group) and 3,797 ± 800 s-1 (C-terminal group) at 20 °C, with fitted minor states of about 2.2% and 1.2%, and a further faster μs process broadens T77-N79.
open_conflicts: Apo exchange model at 20 °C (same human data or same lab): per-residue Carver-Richards fits with populations declared inseparable (2018, r1: S111 1,200 ± 300, L125 2,200 ± 540 s-1) versus a per-residue GUARDD refit at 600/900 MHz (2024 SI Table S1, r38: S111 1,420 ± 100, L125 2,670 ± 500, T164 8,070 ± 3,600 s-1, populations degenerate near 50 ± 20%) versus grouped two-site Arrhenius fits (2023 Table 2, r15: Group II 1,088 ± 180, Group III 3,797 ± 800 with 97.8% and 98.8% major states) versus the 2021 global fit of 125-127/H132/K178/Y205 (2,020 ± 230 s-1, SI Table S4, no evidence row). All agree exchange exists; they disagree on whether it is one, two or many processes and whether the population is measurable.

Human T164S distal effect: 2021 reports lower dispersion amplitudes for residues 125-127, H132, K178, Y205 (r12), while 2024 states that both position-164 swaps induce higher dispersion at distant residues or no effect (r39); both are apo, 20 °C, 900 MHz.

T164 in WT apo: 2018 describes a linear dispersion not suppressed at the highest νCPMG, with no fit (r1), whereas 2023 places T164 in Group III with 3,797 ± 800 and 2024 fits 8,070 ± 3,600; different models for a dispersion that may not reach its plateau.
questions_for_gina: The RelaxDB BLVRB_CPMG curator note says the data are private EZE data with Rex labels from R2(50 Hz) - mean(R2 at 900 and 1000 Hz) > 2 and assignments from BMRB 27462 (apo). Is this the 2018 apo WT 20 °C, 900 MHz TROSY CPMG set (Paukovich 2018), and is the 20 °C apo set in the 2023 Table 2 fit the same recording or a new one?

For the apo minor state, should the atlas carry the 2023 grouped populations (about 1-2% at 20 °C), or leave pB undetermined as the 2018 two-field analysis concluded for fast exchange (the 2024 per-residue refit returns PA near 50 ± 20% for many residues)?
protein_summary.buffer_note: Every BLVRB NMR sample in the rows (2018, 2021, 2023, 2024, and the 2022 inhibitor titrations) was in 50 mM Bis-Tris pH 6.5, 50 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, so the phosphate artefact flagged for other entries does not apply to the samples themselves; phosphate appears only in M9 growth medium and the denaturing Ni-affinity buffer before reverse-phase HPLC and refolding (2018 Methods). No buffer comparison was made, so a Bis-Tris or chloride effect is untested. Other cross-cutting conditions: protein is refolded after denaturing purification, and reverse-phase HPLC was needed because otherwise 1-3% of the enzyme stayed coenzyme-bound (data not shown), a fraction similar in size to the fitted apo minor states; CPMG samples are 2H,15N with unquantified deuteration while R1 samples are protonated; NADPH samples rely on a G6PD/G6P recycling system; bilirubin samples used a commercial isomer mixture. Units: the 2023 Table 2 and 2024 SI Table S1 print kex in 'Hz' (one 2023 cell has no unit); the rows give these values as s-1, read as exchange rates, not converted by 2π.
